static_traits.name: Wang Jing
static_traits.social_status: Having some friends in Sweden to talk with, but not yet fully expressing incompetence and frustration to them; interpersonal relationships appearing distant due to emotional influence
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no psychotherapy received in the past; more prone to losing things during stress or major life changes
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to reflect, fairly cooperative; willing to try recording and practice; having self-deprecating language (like 'I am a forgetful idiot'), harsh on oneself

basic_info.main_problem: 'I always feel like I keep losing things, and recently I even feel like I am losing my mind. This makes me very pained and depressed. The problem worsened after recently losing important items; I think I lose things because I am naturally forgetful and lack organization, so I feel incompetent and unreliable.'
basic_info.core_demands: 'I decided to seek counseling, because the persistent incompetence and sense of frustration from losing things have started affecting my daily functioning and mental health.'
growth_experiences: More prone to losing things during stress or major life changes, often coping with self-blame and a 'sense of incompetence' (a long-standing recurring coping pattern).
Recently moved to Sweden; over the past year took on more responsibilities at the same time (teaching, parenting, volunteer service), significantly increasing role load.
Last week organized a large Red Cross event and completed it smoothly, but has not yet received thanks or recognition; the client feels 'invisible', questioning the meaning of the effort.

core_beliefs: I am not good enough / incompetent
I am a forgetful, stupid, and unreliable person
My value depends on others' recognition

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I lose things, it means I am a forgetful and stupid person, untrustworthy
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Doubling self-blame, trying to compensate by reinforcing organizational and memory skills

special_situations.event: The large Red Cross event organized last week went smoothly, but no one expressed thanks
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others have not explicitly expressed thanks or recognition, it means I did not do well enough and my efforts have no value
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Takes on more tasks and seeks external recognition, but ends up feeling more in need of others' affirmation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: No one values me; my efforts are meaningless

special_situations.event: A student not understanding the course content during class
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If a student momentarily does not understand, it proves I am a terrible teacher
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Wholly negating one's own ability, anxiety rising and avoiding self-care (like skipping yoga class)

special_situations.event: After recently losing an important item, emotions and functioning are markedly affected
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I lose important items at critical moments, it proves I am essentially unreliable and incompetent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeated self-blame, trying to strengthen organizational strategies, but inner negation intensifies

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be seen and recognized, expects one's efforts to be valued by others
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being ignored, being negated as not good enough or unreliable
defense_goal: Avoids being blamed by others through self-criticism and redoubled effort, maintaining a sense of safety in relationships
Lowering the frustration of being judged by others through preemptive self-deprecation

object_relations.self_representation: An ignored 'invisible person' who works hard/not-good-enough contributor
object_relations.object_representation: Indifferent, demanding others/authorities who do not give recognition

object_relations.self_representation: An incompetent person prone to mistakes, needing correction

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When efforts are not yet recognized or thanks from others are not yet received at key moments (e.g. a volunteer event going well but nobody thanking)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Others do not value me; I must not be good enough (transference: projecting the image of important others as 'not approving' onto current others)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Take blame in a self-reproaching tone, downplay others' factors, repeatedly express 'I did not do well/I am not good enough', reduce the need for self-expression.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When small mistakes or errors occur (e.g. losing things, a Student not yet understanding for a moment)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: This is because I am naturally forgetful and lack organizational ability (simplifying a complex situation into an explanation of my own defects)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Use seemingly objective attribution ('I am just forgetful') to jump to conclusions, tone certain, avoiding further exploration of other possible factors.

manifestations: Feeling 'invisible', efforts seen by nobody (no one thanks at volunteer events)
Feeling distant from Family relationships; seeking affirmation instead makes one feel more 'needy'
Questioning 'why should I keep trying' after efforts go unrecognized
Interpreting occasional mistakes as one's own incompetence, negating achievements
outcomes: Decreased motivation and rising Sense of frustration

contact_model.definition: the individual has poor self-Reflection and introspection, containing excessive self-limitation and harsh self-blame, being overly careful and cautious about contact.
manifestations: Frequently using self-derogatory labels (e.g. 'I am a forgetful idiot''I am not good enough')
Quickly blaming oneself when not yet receiving clear affirmation from others, shrinking the need for self-expression

exception_events.target_problem: When taking on important tasks or roles, the client usually worries about not being good enough, fears being overlooked and negated, thus falling into self-blame and helplessness.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Last week a large event organized at the Red Cross went smoothly, overall running Good, demonstrating organizational and coordination ability (though not yet thanked on the spot).
exception_events.reason: Different actions: proactively took on and completed preparation and coordination; different support: already has some friends to talk with in Sweden (though not yet fully confided in, they objectively exist).

positive_force: Has the ability to organize and coordinate large events (volunteer activities held smoothly)
Teaching experience and overall Good teaching feedback (Students' overall performance Good, praised by colleagues)
Has some social support in Sweden (has friends to talk with)
Willing to Reflect and try recording and re-evaluating automatic thoughts
negative_force: Self-labeling and overgeneralization (small mistakes lead to total negation)
Personalization and dependence on external validation (attributing others' not yet expressed thanks to oneself not being good enough)
Avoids self-care when Anxious (e.g. skipping yoga)
Under stress and major life changes, attention lapses increase (more likely to lose things)

target_behavior.behavior: Self-derogatory labels and Excessive self-blame (e.g. 'I am a forgetful idiot''I am not good enough')
antecedent: Important efforts not yet explicitly thanked or recognized (e.g. nobody thanking after volunteer events)
Individual Students not yet understanding the content for a moment in teaching
target_behavior.core_reason: Inner negative core belief ('I am not good enough/not reliable') activated, generalizing occasional mistakes into stable personality flaws, and interpreting events with self-blame.
target_behavior.function: Through self-blame, gains a sense of control and self-drive, and seeks external recognition to confirm self-worth.
target_behavior.consequence: Anxiety and insomnia worsened, avoiding self-care (skipping yoga), Interpersonal relationships affected, Declining work and daily functioning.

target_behavior.behavior: Under stress or major life changes, more prone to losing things
antecedent: Facing major life changes (such as moving, increased role load)
target_behavior.core_reason: In high-pressure and change situations, attention is more easily distracted and omissions increase (the client himself explains it as 'born forgetful, lacking organization').
target_behavior.function: Unintentional behavior, lacking a clear functional purpose.
target_behavior.consequence: Large amounts of time and energy spent looking for things, daily life disrupted, frustration and Self-denial further intensified.
